title: Choosing few indicators and defending the choice

videos.script: Lívia inherits a page for the Monday operations meeting. It has forty numbers on it. {{page}} Eight people read them aloud for half an hour every week, and then nobody decides anything. This lesson is about getting from forty to five, and keeping it there. {{cost}} First, why few. Every number costs time, data and somebody's attention, and a page that shows everything shows nothing. {{score}} Then the method. You start from the objective, ask the questions it raises, and pick the number that answers each one. In your spreadsheet you score ten candidates and watch the easy ones fall to the bottom. {{guard}} Then the guard. Caio's carriers hit their delivery target in two months. The number beside it shows how: damaged deliveries more than doubled. {{defend}} Last, the hard part. Three directors each want one more number on the page. You need a reason for every number, a list for the ones that wait, and a review every quarter.
